summary: Abdur Rehman worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He earned his PhD at the Australian National University under Arthur Llewellyn Basham, also studying under Ahmad Hasan Dani, and served as Assistant Professor of Archaeology at the University of Peshawar (attested 1988).

Abel Bergaigne was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Michel Bréal and Eugène-Louis Hauvette-Besnault. He was a répétiteur at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1869–1877) and a lecturer, then professor of Sanskrit and comparative linguistics, at the Sorbonne.

Abigail I. MacBain specializes in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. She earned an MA at McMaster University, studying under Mark Rowe, James A. Benn, Shayne Clarke, Mark MacWilliams, and Michael Greenwald, and holds a post at the University of Edinburgh (attested 2026).

Abraham Hyacinthe Anquetil-Duperron studied theology at the Sorbonne (~1746–1751), attended the Old Catholic Seminary of Amersfoort, and studied under Dastur Darab. Working in Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and religious studies, he held posts at the Bibliothèque nationale and Institut de France.

Abraham Sachs was a scholar of history, archaeology, and linguistics who studied at Johns Hopkins University (~1933–1937). He was appointed to the Institute for Advanced Study in 1945 and served at Brown University from ~1948 to 1983.

Abraham Valentine Williams Jackson was an Indologist, linguist, and Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar. He studied at Columbia University and the University of Halle-Wittenberg under Edward Washburn Hopkins, later serving at Columbia as a fellow (1883–1890) and professor (1895–1935).
Abraham Zablocki specializes in Tibetology and religious studies. He earned his PhD at Cornell University and held a post at Agnes Scott College (attested 2008).

Achim Bayer specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned his MA under David P. Jackson and his PhD at the University of Hamburg (2005) under Lambert Schmithausen, later working as a research associate at the University of Munich (2004–2006).

Adalbert Bezzenberger was a linguist and Indologist who studied under Theodor Benfey at the University of Göttingen and at the University of Munich. He served as Privatdozent at Göttingen before becoming professor of Sanskrit, prorector, and rector at the University of Königsberg.

Adalbert Kuhn, a linguist and Indologist, studied under Franz Bopp at Humboldt University of Berlin (1833–1837). He taught and served as director at Köllnisches Gymnasium between 1837 and 1870, and was a member of the Prussian and Russian Academies of Sciences.

Adam Bowles specializes in Indology and religious studies. He completed his doctoral studies under Greg Bailey (attested 2004) and served as senior lecturer in Asian Religions at the University of Queensland (attested 2016–2018).

Adam Hardy is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology who studied at Trinity College, Cambridge (~1972–1978). He served as Director at De Montfort University (~1994–2003) and Professor of Asian Architecture at Cardiff University (~2003–2021).

Adam Pearcey is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned his PhD at SOAS University of London under Ulrich Pagel, Nathan W. Hill, and Vincent Tournier, while also studying under numerous traditional Tibetan teachers.

Adam Yuet Chau works in Sinology and religious studies. He studied at Williams College and earned his PhD from Stanford University (2001), later holding posts at Harvard University and the University of Cambridge, where he became Professor of the Anthropology of China.

Adelheid Herrmann-Pfandt works in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. She studied at Erlangen-Nuremberg, Bonn, and Marburg, and has held posts as Käthe-Leichter-Gastprofessorin at the University of Vienna (~2002–2003) and Privatdozentin at the University of Marburg (2009).

Adelheid Mette was an Indologist who completed her doctoral and habilitation studies at the University of Hamburg. She was a professor of Indology at the University of Münster (1971; chair 1988–2000) and held professorial posts at the University of Munich.

Aden Kumler is an art historian who studied at the University of Chicago, University of Toronto, Pontifical Institute of Mediaeval Studies, and Harvard University. She served as Assistant Professor at the University of Chicago (2007) and Professor of Older Art History at the University of Basel (2020).
Adeu Rinpoche was a figure in Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied under traditional teachers Khamtrul Rinpoche, Samten Gyatso, and Chögon Rinpoche.

Adhémard Leclère worked in religious studies, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He served as Résident de France at Kratié in the French Protectorate of Cambodia and was vice-president of the Société Ethnologique de Paris, which he founded.

Adinath Neminath Upadhye was an Indologist who earned his BA and D.Litt. at the University of Mumbai. He taught Prakrit at Rajaram College (1930–1962), served as Professor Emeritus at Shivaji University, and became founding professor and Head of the Jaina Chair at the University of Mysore.
